definitions.gloss: hard of hearing; unable to hear well
definitions.explanation: Set phrase describing someone whose hearing has weakened, typically with age. Literally 'the ears are far'. It is the ordinary, unmarked way to say this in Japanese and is not itself impolite, though it is usually said of another person rather than to them.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}い。
examples.english: My grandmother is hard of hearing.

examples.japanese: {耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}いので、{大|おお}きな{声|こえ}で{話|はな}してください。
examples.english: I don't hear well, so please speak up.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}を{取|と}って{耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}くなってきた。
examples.english: My hearing has been going as I get older.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}いふりをして、{都合|つごう}の{悪|わる}い{話|はなし}を{聞|き}き{流|なが}す。
examples.english: My father pretends to be hard of hearing and lets inconvenient topics pass right by.

notes:
The 〜が{遠|とお}い pattern treats a dulled sense as distance. It conjugates as an i-adjective phrase: {耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}くなる (to grow hard of hearing), {耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}かった (was hard of hearing).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}くなる: to start losing one's hearing
- {少|すこ}し{耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}い: to be a little hard of hearing
- {耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}いふりをする: to pretend not to hear

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {耳|みみ}が{早|はや}い: quick to hear news — same body-part idiom pattern, unrelated meaning
- {耳|みみ}が{痛|いた}い: it hurts to hear — used when criticism hits home
- {難聴|なんちょう}: hearing loss — the clinical term used in medical contexts
